status: SYNTHETIC — first Hermes plugin traces (T17). Live Hermes captures are blocked by the gateway process architecture: CTXVM_TRACE_DIR cannot propagate from the CLI shell to the long-running gateway process where plugins load. Synthetic traces exercise the same declare/fault/turn paths as live captures (echo beats + sustained re-fetch pressure) and are schema-validated and replay-divergence-free.

harness.name: Hermes Agent
harness.tracer: packages/hermes/src/plugin.py (Python port of @ctxvm/node, RFC-0 xCABI JSONL)
harness.wiring: plugin installed at ~/.hermes/plugins/ctxvm-tracer/ via hermes plugins enable; register(ctx) registers on_session_start/pre_tool_call/post_tool_call/pre_llm_call/on_session_end hooks
harness.flush: plugin cleanup on on_session_end → @ctxvm-node-equivalent finish() → RFC-0 JSONL
harness.liveCaptureBlocked: Gateway process isolation prevents CTXVM_TRACE_DIR from propagating from CLI shell to plugin host process. See RR-T17-20261024 §Phase 2.

files.origin: synthetic Hermes session (T17), one scripted user message: read → re-read → edit → fresh read → missing-file error
synthetic Hermes session (T17), five rounds re-reading all five fixture files (25 reads) — sustained re-fetch pressure, pre-eviction thrash shape

limitations: v0 tracer has no eviction path (declared => resident): synthetic drops exercise sustained re-fetch pressure (tool_recall faults) but cannot exhibit page.evict or second-slot paging. The synthetic P-pathology vector in corpus/m1 remains the eviction-shape reference.
Faults are deduped per page·source by the tracer, so repeated re-fetches of the same page yield one tool_recall row each; call.meta carries the per-turn hit/miss pressure.

Synthetic traces are generated by the Python tracer port, not by a live Hermes session. The mapping (hook→tracer) is identical to what the live plugin would produce; only the hook payloads are synthetic.
budgetTokens=120000 is declared headroom bookkeeping (T9 convention), not the provider's measured context window.
